\]
which yields the degree identity $[H:K] = h_K$ and the principal ideal theorem.
This paper studies the subfield structure of $H/K$ in the simplest nontrivial
arithmetic case, where the class number is prime.

\subsection{Main result}
\begin{theorem}[Atomicity of prime-class-number class fields]\label{thm:main}
Let $K$ be a number field with Hilbert class field $H$, and suppose the class
number satisfies $h_K = p$ for a prime $p$. Then $H/K$ has no proper
intermediate fields: for every field $L$ with $K \subseteq L \subseteq H$,
either $L = K$ or $L = H$.
\end{theorem}

The proof factors through: (1) an \emph{arithmetic input}, Artin reciprocity,
converting $h_K$ into $|\Gal(H/K)|$; (2) a \emph{group-theoretic core},
Lagrange's theorem, forbidding proper nontrivial subgroups of a prime-order
group; and (3) the \emph{bridge}, the fundamental theorem of Galois theory,
transporting the subgroup dichotomy into a dichotomy of fields.

\section{Definitions and preliminaries}

Throughout, $K$ is a number field with ring of integers $\OK$.

\begin{definition}[Ideal class group and class number]
The \emph{ideal class group} $\Cl(\OK)$ is the quotient of nonzero fractional
ideals of $\OK$ by nonzero principal fractional ideals. It is finite abelian;
its order $h_K = |\Cl(\OK)|$ is the \emph{class number}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hilbert class field]
The \emph{Hilbert class field} $H$ of $K$ is the maximal unramified abelian
extension of $K$. It is a finite Galois extension of $K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Intermediate field]
Given $H/K$, an \emph{intermediate field} is a field $L$ with
$K \subseteq L \subseteq H$. Such fields form a lattice under inclusion, with
least element $K = \bot$ and greatest element $H = \top$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Artin reciprocity, structural interface]\label{thm:artin}
There is a canonical group isomorphism
$e : \Gal(H/K) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \Cl(\OK)$. Consequently
$|\Gal(H/K)| = h_K$.
\end{theorem}

We treat Theorem~\ref{thm:artin} as the sole arithmetic hypothesis; it is the
only place where the specific nature of the Hilbert class field enters.

\begin{theorem}[Fundamental theorem of Galois theory]\label{thm:galois}
Let $H/K$ be finite Galois with group $G = \Gal(H/K)$. The map
$L \mapsto \Gal(H/L)$ is an order-reversing bijection from the lattice of
intermediate fields of $H/K$ onto the lattice of subgroups of $G$, with inverse
$S \mapsto H^S$. Under it, $K \leftrightarrow G$ and $H \leftrightarrow \{1\}$.
Equivalently there is an order isomorphism

with $\varphi(\bot) = \top$ and $\varphi(\top) = \bot$.
\end{theorem}

\section{The group-theoretic core}

\begin{lemma}[Subgroups of a group of prime order]\label{lem:prime}
Let $G$ be a group with $|G| = p$, $p$ prime. Then every subgroup $S \le G$
satisfies $S = \{1\}$ or $S = G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $|G| = p \neq 0$, $G$ is finite. By Lagrange's theorem, $|S|$ divides
$|G| = p$. As $p$ is prime, $|S| \in \{1, p\}$. If $|S| = 1$ then $S = \{1\}$;

cardinality, $S = G$. In either case $S \in \{\{1\}, G\}$.
\end{proof}

Lemma~\ref{lem:prime} says the subgroup lattice of a prime-order group is the
two-element chain $\{1\} < G$, with no intermediate nodes. The divisibility
proof above is self-contained and uses no generator.
\end{remark}

\section{Proof of the main theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main2}
Let $K$ be a number field and $H/K$ a finite Galois extension equipped with the
Artin reciprocity isomorphism $e : \Gal(H/K) \cong \Cl(\OK)$ characterizing $H$
as the Hilbert class field. If the class number of $K$ equals a prime $p$, then
every intermediate field $L$ with $K \subseteq L \subseteq H$ satisfies $L = K$
or $L = H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $G = \Gal(H/K)$.

\emph{Step 1 (prime order).} The bijection $e$ gives

\emph{Step 2 (transport).} Let $\varphi$ be the order-reversing isomorphism of
Theorem~\ref{thm:galois}, with $\varphi(\bot)=\top$, $\varphi(\top)=\bot$
(where $\bot = K,\top = H$ on fields and $\bot = \{1\}, \top = G$ on subgroups).

Lemma~\ref{lem:prime}, $\varphi(L) = \{1\}$ or $\varphi(L) = G$.

$\varphi(\bot) = \top$ and $\varphi$ is injective, $L = \bot = K$. In both cases
$L \in \{K, H\}$.

nontrivial tower or compositum of smaller extensions of $K$ inside $H$.

Primality is essential. If $h_K$ is composite, $\Cl(\OK)$ has a proper

For the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one, $H = K$; the tower

\textbf{Atomicity decision.} Compute $h_K$; test whether it is prime; report

enumerate its subgroups and reverse the order; the resulting poset is the
intermediate-field lattice of $H/K$. The number of intermediate fields equals
the number of subgroups of $\Cl(\OK)$: $2$ for $\Z/p$, $3$ for $\Z/p^2$, and

\section{Discussion}

Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is a rigidity statement: prime class number forces the
class field to be an indecomposable atom. Its interest lies in the clarity of
the translation --- an arithmetic question about sub-extensions is converted by
Artin reciprocity into a group-theoretic question about subgroups, settled by
Lagrange's theorem. The subfield lattice of $H/K$ always mirrors (as order
dual) the subgroup lattice of $\Cl(\OK)$, so arithmetic of towers over $K$ is
encoded in finite group theory. This is a fully explicit instance of the
class-field-theoretic program generalizing Kronecker--Weber.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Squarefree rigidity]
$H/K$ has a distributive (Boolean) subfield lattice, a product of prime layers,
precisely when $h_K$ is squarefree; the first non-distributive behaviour
appears at the smallest square factor.

\begin{conjecture}[Reciprocity fingerprint]
If $H/K$ is abelian of prime degree $p$, primes of $K$ split completely in $H$
exactly along a single ray-class condition of index $p$, governed by one
primitive character of order $p$, with no coarser condition sufficing.

The failure of prime-degree rigidity is controlled by the $p$-part of the class
group: the number of independent degree-$p$ intermediate (genus) layers equals
the $p$-rank of $\Cl(\OK)$.
\end{conjecture}

\section{Conclusion}
A number field with prime class number has an atomic Hilbert class field, by
combining Artin reciprocity, Lagrange's theorem, and the fundamental theorem of
Galois theory. The result anchors a spectrum of rigidity phenomena --- atomic
prime layers, Boolean squarefree layerings, and higher-rank genus richness ---
all governed by the subgroup lattice of the ideal class group.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return True iff n is a prime number (trial division)."""
    if n < 2:
        return False
    i = 2
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
        i += 1
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finite abelian groups modelling class groups Cl(O_K)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A finite abelian group is represented by its invariant factors, e.g.
#   Z/2            -> (2,)
#   Z/4            -> (4,)
#   Z/2 x Z/2      -> (2, 2)
#   Z/2 x Z/6      -> (2, 6)
# Elements are tuples (x_0, ..., x_{k-1}) with 0 <= x_i < factor_i, added
# componentwise modulo the respective factor.
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Element = Tuple[int, ...]


def group_elements(factors: Group) -> List[Element]:
    """All elements of the abelian group Z/factors[0] x ... x Z/factors[k-1]."""
    ranges = [range(f) for f in factors]
    return [tuple(e) for e in product(*ranges)]


def add(a: Element, b: Element, factors: Group) -> Element:
    """Group addition modulo the invariant factors."""
    return tuple((x + y) % f for x, y, f in zip(a, b, factors))


def subgroup_generated(gens: List[Element], factors: Group) -> frozenset:
    """The subgroup generated by a list of elements (closure under +)."""
    identity = tuple(0 for _ in factors)
    elems = {identity}
    frontier = list(elems)
    while frontier:
        new_frontier = []
        for x in frontier:
            for g in gens:
                y = add(x, g, factors)
                if y not in elems:
                    elems.add(y)
                    new_frontier.append(y)
        frontier = new_frontier
    return frozenset(elems)

    elems = group_elements(factors)
    seen = set()
    subgroups: List[frozenset] = []
    # Generate subgroups as closures of subsets of generators. For small groups
    # it suffices to close every subset of elements; we do this incrementally by
    # closing single elements then merging, which stays cheap for |G| small.
    # Start with the trivial subgroup.
    trivial = subgroup_generated([], factors)
    subgroups.append(trivial)
    seen.add(trivial)

    changed = True

        changed = False
        for H in list(subgroups):

from itertools import product
from math import gcd
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return True iff n is a prime number (trial division)."""
    if n < 2:
        return False
    i = 2
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
        i += 1
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finite abelian groups modelling class groups Cl(O_K)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A finite abelian group is represented by its invariant factors, e.g.
#   Z/2            -> (2,)
#   Z/4            -> (4,)
#   Z/2 x Z/2      -> (2, 2)
#   Z/2 x Z/6      -> (2, 6)
# Elements are tuples (x_0, ..., x_{k-1}) with 0 <= x_i < factor_i, added
# componentwise modulo the respective factor.
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Element = Tuple[int, ...]


def group_elements(factors: Group) -> List[Element]:
    """All elements of the abelian group Z/factors[0] x ... x Z/factors[k-1]."""
    ranges = [range(f) for f in factors]
    return [tuple(e) for e in product(*ranges)]


def add(a: Element, b: Element, factors: Group) -> Element:
    """Group addition modulo the invariant factors."""
    return tuple((x + y) % f for x, y, f in zip(a, b, factors))


def subgroup_generated(gens: List[Element], factors: Group) -> frozenset:
    """The subgroup generated by a list of elements (closure under +)."""
    identity = tuple(0 for _ in factors)
    elems = {identity}
    frontier = list(elems)
    while frontier:
        new_frontier = []
        for x in frontier:
            for g in gens:
                y = add(x, g, factors)
                if y not in elems:
                    elems.add(y)
                    new_frontier.append(y)
        frontier = new_frontier
    return frozenset(elems)


def all_subgroups(factors: Group) -> List[frozenset]:
    """Enumerate every subgroup of the finite abelian group (small groups)."""
    elems = group_elements(factors)
    seen = set()
    subgroups: List[frozenset] = []
    # Generate subgroups as closures of subsets of generators. For small groups
    # it suffices to close every subset of elements; we do this incrementally by
    # closing single elements then merging, which stays cheap for |G| small.
    # Start with the trivial subgroup.
    trivial = subgroup_generated([], factors)
    subgroups.append(trivial)
    seen.add(trivial)
    # Grow: repeatedly adjoin one element to each known subgroup.
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for H in list(subgroups):
            for g in elems:
                gens = list(H) + [g]
                new = subgroup_generated(gens, factors)
                if new not in seen:
                    seen.add(new)
                    subgroups.append(new)
                    changed = True
    return subgroups

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_atomic(class_number: int) -> bool:
    """
    Decide whether the Hilbert class field H/K is atomic (no proper
    intermediate fields), given only the class number h_K = [H:K].

    By the main theorem this is equivalent to h_K being prime.
    """
    return is_prime(class_number)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def num_intermediate_fields(factors: Group) -> int:
    """
    Number of intermediate fields of H/K (including K and H), which equals the
    number of subgroups of the class group Cl(O_K) via the Galois correspondence.
    """
    return len(all_subgroups(factors))


def group_order(factors: Group) -> int:
    """Order of the abelian group = class number h_K."""
    n = 1
    for f in factors:
        n *= f
    return n


def is_cyclic(factors: Group) -> bool:
    """A product Z/f_0 x ... is cyclic iff the factors are pairwise coprime."""
    for i in range(len(factors)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(factors)):
            if gcd(factors[i], factors[j]) != 1:

    return True

open NumberField

theorem subgroup_eq_bot_or_top_of_prime_card

    (S : Subgroup G) : S = ⊥ ∨ S = ⊤ := by
  have hfin : Finite G := by

    exact Nat.finite_of_card_ne_zero this
  have hdvd : Nat.card S ∣ Nat.card G := Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card S
  rw [hG] at hdvd
  rcases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd _ hdvd with h1 | hpc
  · exact Or.inl (Subgroup.eq_bot_of_card_le S (le_of_eq h1))
  · exact Or.inr (Subgroup.eq_top_of_card_eq S (by rw [hpc, hG]))

theorem hilbertClassFieldNoIntermediates

    (H : Type*) [Field H] [Algebra K H] [FiniteDimensional K H] [IsGalois K H]
    (e : (H ≃ₐ[K] H) ≃* ClassGroup (RingOfIntegers K))

    have h2 : Nat.card (H ≃ₐ[K] H) = Nat.card (ClassGroup (RingOfIntegers K)) :=

    apply OrderDual.ofDual.injective
    rw [hbot]; rfl

Numerical demonstration of the atomicity theorem for prime-class-number
Hilbert class fields.

Main theorem (in plain mathematical terms):
    Let K be a number field with Hilbert class field H (the maximal unramified
    abelian extension of K). Artin reciprocity gives a canonical isomorphism
        Gal(H/K)  ~=  Cl(O_K)      (the ideal class group),
    hence [H:K] = h_K, the class number. If h_K is PRIME, then H/K has no proper
    intermediate fields: every field L with K <= L <= H equals K or H.

The subfield lattice of H/K is (as an order dual) exactly the subgroup lattice
of the class group Cl(O_K). This file demonstrates the theorem entirely at the
level of finite abelian groups: we model class groups by their invariant
factors, enumerate the subgroup lattice, and confirm that the number of
intermediate fields equals the number of subgroups -- and that this number is 2
(atomic) precisely when the class number is prime and the group is cyclic.

All functions are self-contained; only the Python standard library is used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from math import gcd
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return True iff n is a prime number (trial division)."""
    if n < 2:
        return False
    i = 2
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
        i += 1
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finite abelian groups modelling class groups Cl(O_K)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A finite abelian group is represented by its invariant factors, e.g.
#   Z/2            -> (2,)
#   Z/4            -> (4,)
#   Z/2 x Z/2      -> (2, 2)
#   Z/2 x Z/6      -> (2, 6)
# Elements are tuples (x_0, ..., x_{k-1}) with 0 <= x_i < factor_i, added
# componentwise modulo the respective factor.
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Element = Tuple[int, ...]


def group_elements(factors: Group) -> List[Element]:
    """All elements of the abelian group Z/factors[0] x ... x Z/factors[k-1]."""
    ranges = [range(f) for f in factors]
    return [tuple(e) for e in product(*ranges)]


def add(a: Element, b: Element, factors: Group) -> Element:
    """Group addition modulo the invariant factors."""
    return tuple((x + y) % f for x, y, f in zip(a, b, factors))


def subgroup_generated(gens: List[Element], factors: Group) -> frozenset:
    """The subgroup generated by a list of elements (closure under +)."""
    identity = tuple(0 for _ in factors)
    elems = {identity}
    frontier = list(elems)
    while frontier:
        new_frontier = []
        for x in frontier:
            for g in gens:
                y = add(x, g, factors)
                if y not in elems:
                    elems.add(y)
                    new_frontier.append(y)
        frontier = new_frontier
    return frozenset(elems)


def all_subgroups(factors: Group) -> List[frozenset]:
    """Enumerate every subgroup of the finite abelian group (small groups)."""
    elems = group_elements(factors)
    seen = set()
    subgroups: List[frozenset] = []
    # Generate subgroups as closures of subsets of generators. For small groups
    # it suffices to close every subset of elements; we do this incrementally by
    # closing single elements then merging, which stays cheap for |G| small.
    # Start with the trivial subgroup.
    trivial = subgroup_generated([], factors)
    subgroups.append(trivial)
    seen.add(trivial)
    # Grow: repeatedly adjoin one element to each known subgroup.
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for H in list(subgroups):
            for g in elems:
                gens = list(H) + [g]
                new = subgroup_generated(gens, factors)
                if new not in seen:
                    seen.add(new)
                    subgroups.append(new)
                    changed = True
    return subgroups


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm A: atomicity decision
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def is_atomic(class_number: int) -> bool:
    """
    Decide whether the Hilbert class field H/K is atomic (no proper
    intermediate fields), given only the class number h_K = [H:K].

    By the main theorem this is equivalent to h_K being prime.
    """
    return is_prime(class_number)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm B: intermediate-field lattice via the class group
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def num_intermediate_fields(factors: Group) -> int:
    """
    Number of intermediate fields of H/K (including K and H), which equals the
    number of subgroups of the class group Cl(O_K) via the Galois correspondence.
    """
    return len(all_subgroups(factors))


def group_order(factors: Group) -> int:
    """Order of the abelian group = class number h_K."""
    n = 1
    for f in factors:
        n *= f
    return n


def is_cyclic(factors: Group) -> bool:
    """A product Z/f_0 x ... is cyclic iff the factors are pairwise coprime."""
    for i in range(len(factors)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(factors)):
            if gcd(factors[i], factors[j]) != 1:
                return False
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Worked examples: imaginary quadratic fields K = Q(sqrt(d))
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (discriminant/field label, class group invariant factors) from classical tables.
IMAGINARY_QUADRATIC: Dict[str, Group] = {
    "Q(sqrt(-1))": (1,),          # h = 1  (trivial group)
    "Q(sqrt(-5))": (2,),          # h = 2  prime -> atomic
    "Q(sqrt(-6))": (2,),          # h = 2  prime -> atomic
    "Q(sqrt(-23))": (3,),         # h = 3  prime -> atomic (cyclic cubic)
    "Q(sqrt(-31))": (3,),         # h = 3  prime -> atomic
    "Q(sqrt(-14))": (4,),         # h = 4  cyclic Z/4 -> one intermediate field
    "Q(sqrt(-21))": (2, 2),       # h = 4  Z/2 x Z/2 -> genus layering
    "Q(sqrt(-47))": (5,),         # h = 5  prime -> atomic
}


def describe_field(label: str, factors: Group) -> str:
    """Human-readable one-line summary of a field's class-field structure."""
    h = group_order(factors)
    n_sub = num_intermediate_fields(factors)
    n_proper = n_sub - 2  # exclude K and H
    atomic = is_atomic(h)
    grp = "trivial" if h == 1 else " x ".join(f"Z/{f}" for f in factors)
    verdict = (
        "H = K (nothing to extend)" if h == 1
        else "ATOMIC: no intermediate fields" if atomic
        else f"{n_proper} proper intermediate field(s)"
    )
    return (
        f"{label:16s} h_K={h:<2d} Cl(O_K)={grp:14s} "
        f"subgroups={n_sub:<2d}  ->  {verdict}"
    )


def main() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("Atomicity of prime-class-number Hilbert class fields")
    print("=" * 78)
    print()
    print("Theorem: h_K prime  <=>  H/K has NO proper intermediate fields.")
    print("The intermediate-field lattice of H/K mirrors the subgroup lattice")
    print("of the class group Cl(O_K) (Artin reciprocity + Galois correspondence).")
    print()

    print("-" * 78)
    print("Worked examples over imaginary quadratic fields:")
    print("-" * 78)
    for label, factors in IMAGINARY_QUADRATIC.items():
        print(describe_field(label, factors))

    print("-" * 78)
    print("Cross-check: prime order  <=>  exactly 2 subgroups  <=>  atomic")
    print("-" * 78)
    for factors in [(2,), (3,), (5,), (7,), (4,), (6,), (9,), (2, 2), (3, 3)]:
        h = group_order(factors)

        atomic_by_theorem = is_atomic(h)
        atomic_by_lattice = (n_sub == 2)
        cyclic = is_cyclic(factors)
        assert atomic_by_theorem == atomic_by_lattice, "theorem/lattice mismatch!"
        grp = " x ".join(f"Z/{f}" for f in factors)
        print(
            f"Cl={grp:12s} h={h:<3d} #subgroups={n_sub:<2d} "
            f"cyclic={str(cyclic):5s} atomic={atomic_by_lattice}"
        )
    print()

    print("-" * 78)
    print("Subgroup counts for standard shapes (sanity):")
    print("-" * 78)
    print(f"  Z/p        -> {num_intermediate_fields((5,))} subgroups (expected 2)")
    print(f"  Z/p^2      -> {num_intermediate_fields((9,))} subgroups (expected 3)")
    print(f"  Z/p x Z/p  -> {num_intermediate_fields((3, 3))} subgroups "

    print()
    print("All assertions passed: prime class number is exactly atomicity.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
